verdict.line: You lose if you let Jax farm Empower autos on your face at levels 1-3; you win every all-in from level 6 onward if Wither connects first.

brief.thesis: Jax's entire early game runs on W (Empower) cooldown resets and E (Counter Strike) baiting your Q (Siphoning Strike), while your entire game runs on stacking that same Q. Whoever controls the trade range — inside Jax's 700-range Q (Leap Strike) or outside it — decides whether this is a stack-farming lane or a feeding lane. The 52% Nasus win rate over 1848 games says this is winnable, but OP.GG's own lane-advantage call to Jax means you have to fight for that range, not assume it.

theirWindow.when: Empower is up and he's in melee range
theirWindow.what: His next auto or Leap Strike hits hard and splashes nearby — do not stand still and trade autos, back off a step or eat it and reset with Q (Siphoning Strike) instead of chaining autos.

yourWindow.when: Empower is down and E (Counter Strike) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: This is your real trade window — walk up, land Q (Siphoning Strike) for the stack and the damage, then disengage before Empower comes back up.

start.why: 52.6% win rate over 1304 games — the extra healing from autos and the 8% damage reduction from minions directly counters Jax's early Empower poke and Leap Strike dive attempts.

boots.why: 50.5% win rate over 735 games — Jax's R (Relentless Assault) scales attack speed, and the flat physical damage reduction on multiple-hit sources cuts his auto-reset damage specifically.

core.why: 61.5% win rate as the lead item in the top build path over 361 games — the attack speed and on-hit damage accelerate your Q (Siphoning Strike) stacking rate, which is the entire win condition against a champion who scales off items, not stacks.
Second in the top path — the armor directly answers Jax's auto-attack and Leap Strike physical damage, and the attack speed slow weakens his Empower reset tempo.
Completes the 61.5%-win-rate path over 361 games — boosted healing turns your passive (Soul Eater) lifesteal and E (Spirit Fire) sustain into real lane survivability against his all-in windows.

runes.keystoneWhy: Run on 54% of Nasus players in this matchup at 52% pick rate — the movement speed burst lets you step into Q (Siphoning Strike) range and immediately retreat before Empower or Leap Strike punishes you, and the heal offsets his early poke.

summoners.why: Run on 47.9% of games at a 52% win rate — Ghost lets you close the gap on Jax's dash-reliant kit for Q stacks or disengage from his all-in, while Teleport lets you commit fully to farming Q stacks without giving up map presence.

playing.title: Farm Q, don't fight autos
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to prioritize Q (Siphoning Strike) stacking over trading — every stack compounds your late game, and Jax's Empower makes raw auto trades a loss for you before level 6.

playing.title: Track Empower, not just health
playing.detail: Jax's W (Empower) has a 7/6/5/4/3s cooldown that only gets shorter — if you see the empowered auto indicator up, do not contest melee range, let him waste it on a minion or walk away.

playing.title: Use Wither to deny his engage
playing.detail: W (Wither) slows his Movement and Attack Speed over time at 700 range — cast it the moment he commits Leap Strike (Q) toward you so his follow-up autos and Empower land slower and you can walk out.

playing.title: Never Q into his E stance
playing.detail: Counter Strike (E) dodges all incoming basic attacks and stuns on a 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown — Q (Siphoning Strike) is a basic attack-based strike, so throwing it while he's in the stance window just feeds him the stun; wait out the animation.

playing.title: All-in only with R up
playing.detail: From level 6 on, R (Fury of the Sands) gives you the health and sustained damage to win extended trades — do not commit to a long fight on cooldown, since without R your sustain can't out-race his Empower-reset damage.

playing.title: Spirit Fire before you commit
playing.detail: E (Spirit Fire) reduces armor on anyone standing in it on a 12s cooldown — drop it under Jax before an all-in so your Q damage and autos scale up for the fight.

playing.title: Respect his solo-kill power to level 5
playing.detail: The data shows Jax holds the solo-kill advantage, driven by Leap Strike (8/5s cooldown at later ranks) plus Empower burst — play for stacks and sustain through level 5 rather than contesting all-ins you can't yet win.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing advice are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Pay attention to Jax’s (P) and Conqueror stack count while keeping your distance. Focus foremost on farming with [Q], and use Wither [W] to create some distance when Jax closes in.
